Options: 
A. magnitude of the resting potentials of their membranes
B. size and structure of their cells
C. ability to regenerate after damage
D. speed at which they transmit signals
E. number of axons each cell possesses
F. ions involved in their action potentials
G. degree of sensitivity to external stimuli
H. length of their refractory periods
I. location of their synapses
J. types of energy they transduce

    *   **Cochlea (Ear):** Receptors are mechanoreceptors (hair cells). They transduce sound/mechanical energy into electrical signals.
    *   **Similarities:** Both perform transduction. Both generate graded potentials that trigger action potentials in neurons. Both have resting potentials. Both regenerate (hair cells mostly don't actually regenerate well in adults, rods/cones regenerate limited neogenesis or replacement cells, but the key functional distinction is usually about the stimulus).
    *   **Differences:**

        *   **Option B (Size/Structure):** Photoreceptors are single cell types (rods/cones). Hair cells are modified neurons/specialized cell bodies on top of nerve endings. Morphology differs, but the question asks for "Functionally".
        *   **Option C (Regeneration):** Hair cells do not regenerate well (though some studies suggest new hair cells can form in zebrafish, in humans they don't). Rods/Cones degenerate and are not replaced by new cells. This is a structural/functional difference, but often cited as a unique limitation of hair cells. However, the transduction mechanism is the core functional divergence.
        *   **Option D (Speed):** Signal transmission speed (myelination/axonal conduction) varies per nerve fibers, not necessarily the receptor cell type itself primarily.
        *   **Option E (Number of axons):** Usually single receptor to single bipolar process in wireslike transmission, but hair cells synapse with many bipolar pool cells. This varies.
        *   **Option F (Ions):** Both sodium/potassium play roles. Mechanotransduction involves many channels (Piezo, TMC, TRP) + mechanically gated, Phototransduction involves G-protein cascades and cGMP channels (cGMP-gated Na/Ca).
        *   **Option G (Sensitivity):** Rods are very sensitive; hair cells vary frequency. This is somewhat functional.
        *   **Option H (Refractory periods):** Both neurons have them.
        *   **Option I (Location of synapses):** Photoreceptors synapse with bipolar cells. Hair cells release neurotransmitters in the stereocilia base to afferent/deefferent neurons.
        *   **Option J (Types of energy they transduce):** This is the definition of a sensory receptor.
            *   Retina = Photoreceptors. They transduce Light (electromagnetic radiation).
            *   Cochlea = Mechanoreceptors. They transduce Mechanical energy (pressure/vibration of sound).
